title: How Much Does It Cost to Replace a Car Key in Oklahoma City?
excerpt: How much does a car key replacement cost in Oklahoma City? Real 2026 price ranges by key type — basic, transponder, and smart fob — plus how to avoid overpaying.
bodyText: How much does it cost to replace a car key in Oklahoma City? Straight answer: a basic metal key usually runs about $50 to $100, a transponder chip key about $120 to $250, and a smart push-to-start fob about $200 to $450 or more on luxury vehicles. What you pay comes down mostly to your key type and your vehicle, and you get your exact price up front on the phone before we dispatch. The three kinds of car keys: basic metal key $50-$100 (no chip, just cut), transponder chip key $120-$250 (cut plus program the chip to your immobilizer), and smart key or push-to-start fob $200-$450+ (specialized equipment, secure programming, more time). Why two people pay different prices: your key type, make model and year, newer vehicles that need paid dealer-level software and per-vehicle security tokens we buy from the automaker, distance since we come to you, spare vs all-keys-lost, and timing for after-hours emergency fees. Locksmith vs the dealership: for most vehicles a mobile locksmith is faster and cheaper, you skip the tow and the multi-day wait. The cheapest car key is the spare you make today, a duplicate is a fraction of an all-keys-lost replacement. If a price sounds too cheap to be real it is, the $19 car key ad is the classic bait and switch. Our promise: the price before the work, we quote your exact price on the phone and that is what you pay. We cover the OKC metro: OKC, Edmond, Norman, Moore, Yukon, Warr Acres, and we come to you. Call 405-870-5397. Interest-free payment plans available.

title: Locked Out of Your Car in OKC? Exactly What to Do (and What Not to Do)
excerpt: Locked out in Oklahoma City? Exactly what to do, the costly mistakes to avoid, and what to expect when you call a licensed local locksmith.
bodyText: Locked out of your car in OKC? Here is exactly what to do, in order. First take a breath. Before anything else: if a child or a pet is locked inside, especially in Oklahoma heat, call 911 right now. An overheating car is an emergency. If it is just you and your keys on the wrong side of the glass, do it the smart way. Step 1: check every door and the trunk. Do a full lap. Step 2: got roadside coverage or insurance? Call us first. You do not have to wait on a dispatched third party. Pay for the lockout and we give you an itemized invoice you can submit for reimbursement. Most lockout coverage plans reimburse you whether their dispatcher sent someone or you called a licensed locksmith yourself. If you have a spare key nearby, grab it. Step 3: call a licensed local locksmith. A proper car lockout takes minutes. Look for a real licensed locksmith, a local number and real business, and someone who tells you the price before they start. What NOT to do: do not use a coat hanger or slim jim. Modern cars have airbag wiring, sensors, lock actuators, and the window regulator inside the door. A slip can set off a side airbag. Do not pry the window or door frame. Do not call the first nineteen dollar locksmith ad you see, that is the classic bait and switch. What it actually costs: you will know the exact price up front, before we dispatch a technician. A standard car lockout is one of the most affordable jobs we do. We cover the Oklahoma City metro, OKC, Edmond, Norman, Moore, Yukon, Warr Acres, and we come to you. We can help push to start and keyless vehicles too. Call 405-870-5397.
